title: Windows Cisco Secure Endpoint Unblock File Via Sfc
exclusions: Sees only Windows endpoints that log process creation. If the attacker stops logging first, or uses a method other than `sfc.exe`, pair this with the Secure Endpoint connector heartbeat check in the Secure Endpoint console.
evidence: Saved alert results with host, user, command line, and parent process, plus the change or support ticket that explains each hit.

controlTest.positiveScenario: On a test host with the Secure Endpoint connector, run `"C:\Program Files\Cisco\AMP\<version>\sfc.exe" -unblock` against a test block as an administrator. Sysmon logs Event ID 1, and the search returns one row with the `-unblock` command line.
controlTest.negativeScenario: On the same host run `sfc.exe /scannow` from `C:\Windows\System32` as an administrator. Sysmon logs the process, but the path exclusion drops it and the search returns no row.

dataSources: Process creation events from Windows endpoints running the Cisco Secure Endpoint connector: Sysmon Event ID 1 (`source=XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational`, fields `Image`, `CommandLine`, `ParentImage`, `User`) or Security Event ID 4688 with command-line logging, normalised to `Endpoint.Processes`.
app: Splunk Add-on for Sysmon ([Splunkbase 5709](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/5709)) for Sysmon Event ID 1, or Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows ([Splunkbase 742](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/742)) for Security Event ID 4688 with command-line auditing. Either feed must be mapped to the CIM Endpoint data model for the accelerated variant.
spl:
index=sysmon source="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 Image="*\\sfc.exe" CommandLine="* -unblock *" NOT (Image="*:\\Windows\\System32\\*" OR Image="*:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\*" OR Image="*:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\*")
| stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(CommandLine) as process values(ParentImage) as parent_process values(User) as user by dest Image
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
description: Finds runs of the Cisco Secure Endpoint connector's own `sfc.exe` (not the Windows System File Checker in System32) with the command-line switch that removes blocks the connector has placed (`-unblock`). Returns the host, user, full command line, and parent process.
value: Unblocking lets a file or process that Secure Endpoint quarantined or blocked run again. An attacker with admin rights uses it to bring their payload back; a well-meaning admin uses it to undo a detection without investigating it. Both need a second look.
implementation: Collect Sysmon Event ID 1 (or Security 4688 with command lines) from Windows endpoints with the Secure Endpoint connector. Schedule every 15 minutes and alert on every hit; confirm each one against a change or support ticket.
visualization: Alert table: firstTime, lastTime, dest, user, process, parent_process. Supporting panel: 30-day count of connector tamper commands by host (bar chart).
cimSpl:
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
  where Processes.process_name="sfc.exe" Processes.process="* -unblock *" NOT Processes.process_path IN ("*:\\Windows\\System32\\*", "*:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\*", "*:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\*")
  by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_path Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process
| rename Processes.* as *
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
dataModelAcceleration: Enable acceleration on the CIM Endpoint data model, dataset Processes, over the endpoint process index before using the tstats variant.

references.title: Cisco Secure Endpoint: command-line switches for the Windows connector

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Support and upgrade work** — Cisco TAC procedures and connector upgrades use these switches. They run from an administrator account on a known jump host or software deployment tool; check the parent process.

2. **Software deployment tools** — SCCM, Intune, or similar tools that reinstall the connector run `sfc.exe` as SYSTEM from their agent process.

**Suppression:** a lookup of approved parent processes and maintenance windows; no blanket suppression by host.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Add-on for Sysmon (Splunkbase 5709) or Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742) on the search heads and on the Universal Forwarders of the Windows endpoints.
• Sysmon installed on the endpoints with a configuration that logs Event ID 1 (process creation) including the command line, or Windows audit policy *Audit Process Creation* plus *Include command line in process creation events* for Event ID 4688.
• An index for endpoint process data (this page uses `index=sysmon`), a role with `srchIndexesAllowed` on it for the SOC, and, for the accelerated variant, the CIM Endpoint data model accelerated over that index.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
• On each Windows forwarder enable `[WinEventLog://Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational]` with `renderXml = true` and `index = sysmon`; the Sysmon add-on parses it and maps it to `Endpoint.Processes`.
• The Secure Endpoint connector installs its own `sfc.exe` under `C:\Program Files\Cisco\AMP\<version>\`; the Windows System File Checker with the same name lives in System32, which is why the search excludes System32, SysWOW64, and WinSxS paths.
• Check the data this search needs: run `index=sysmon EventCode=1 Image="*\\Cisco\\AMP\\*" | stats count by Image` over 7 days and confirm connector processes appear.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=sysmon source="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 Image="*\\sfc.exe" CommandLine="* -unblock *" NOT (Image="*:\\Windows\\System32\\*" OR Image="*:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\*" OR Image="*:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\*")
| stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(CommandLine) as process values(ParentImage) as parent_process values(User) as user by dest Image
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
```

Understanding this SPL
• The first line limits Sysmon process creation to `sfc.exe` outside the Windows system folders, which leaves the Secure Endpoint connector binary.
• `CommandLine="* -unblock *"` matches the switch that removes blocks the connector has placed (`-unblock`).
• `stats` per host and binary keeps the full command line, user, and parent process for the reviewer.

Accelerated variant over the CIM data model:
```spl
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
  where Processes.process_name="sfc.exe" Processes.process="* -unblock *" NOT Processes.process_path IN ("*:\\Windows\\System32\\*", "*:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\*", "*:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\*")
  by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_path Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process
| rename Processes.* as *
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
```
• The tstats variant runs the same logic on the accelerated Endpoint.Processes dataset and works for any EDR or Windows feed mapped to CIM.

Step 3 — Validate
• Compare with the Secure Endpoint console (Management > Computers) for the host on the alert row: the connector should show as stopped, uninstalled, or with a changed state at the alert time.
• Confirm in Sysmon on the host (Event Viewer > Applications and Services Logs > Microsoft > Windows > Sysmon) that the Event ID 1 with this command line exists.
• Run `index=sysmon EventCode=1 | timechart span=1h count by host limit=10` over 7 days; hosts that stop reporting may be the ones being tampered with.

Step 4 — Operationalize
• Schedule every 15 minutes over the last 20 minutes and throttle on `dest` for 1 hour.
• Route to the SOC. If there is no ticket, isolate the host from the Secure Endpoint console or the network and collect the process tree.
• Enable Connector Protection in the Secure Endpoint policy so these switches require a password; this detection then catches attempts by anyone who has it.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• No rows from the raw search and no Sysmon events: check the forwarder's `inputs.conf` has `[WinEventLog://Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational]` enabled with `renderXml = true`.
• Raw search returns rows but the tstats variant does not: the Endpoint data model is not accelerated over `index=sysmon`, or the `cim_Endpoint_indexes` macro does not include that index.
• `CommandLine` is empty on Event ID 4688: command-line auditing is not enabled by Group Policy. Enable it or use Sysmon.
• Every Windows `sfc.exe` run shows up: the path exclusion did not match because `Image` uses a different drive letter or a short path. Check `Image` on one event.
grandmaExplanation: We alert when someone tells the security software to stop blocking something it caught, so a person checks that it is really safe.
